query: What is the main bytecode evaluation loop that executes Python bytecode instructions?

matches.reason: This is CPython's core bytecode interpreter entry point: it sets up the opcode dispatch machinery (computed-goto jump table or switch) and drives execution by including the generated instruction-dispatch body.

Auto-generated (from bytecodes.c) C code implementing every bytecode instruction's TARGET label body; this is #include'd directly into _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault and is literally the dispatch loop's instruction logic.

The authoritative DSL source of truth defining each bytecode instruction's semantics, from which generated_cases.c.h (and ceval.c's tier-1 loop body) is mechanically generated by Tools/cases_generator.
